blocks.text: When you click the Clipboard icon ( ) within a privileged console, the Clipboard window appears. In this window, you can copy and paste within the privileged console based on the consoles policies that you have set. If you enable the Clipboard Copy option, you can copy functions from Privileged Remote Access (PRA) to your local system. If you enable the Clipboard Paste option, you can paste functions from your local system to PRA. If you have multiple privileged consoles open, copied text is carried over to all of the Clipboard-enabled privileged consoles.
Keep the following in mind when using Clipboard:

blocks.item: You can only use Clipboard operations when the selected protocol and remote OS allow it.
You cannot copy and paste non-ASCII characters with the Clipboard feature if the privileged console is using a VNC protocol, RealVNC protocol, or an SSH protocol.
Clipboard operations between a non-Windows OS and a Windows OS can lead to additional newline characters, as Windows uses a different newline character format.

blocks.text: Clipboard options are disabled by default, but you can still click the Clipboard icon.
To learn more about PRA, see Understanding Privileged Remote Access. To set up PRA, see Step-by-Step Configuration Guide for Privileged Remote Access.

Certain browsers support the Clipboard copy function in a privileged console using your own keyboard. To learn more, see Browser Behavior. From your own keyboard, use the keys associated with copying for the related machine. When your browser doesn't allow the Clipboard copy function with your keyboard, use the following steps:

blocks.item: Highlight the information you want to copy from the privileged console.
Click the Clipboard icon at the bottom of the screen.

blocks.text: The Clipboard window appears.
When you enable the Clipboard features in a consoles policy, a new session must be started before the Clipboard permissions take effect. Refreshing the page also refreshes the permissions.
The copied text appears in the Clipboard window. To remove the copied text, click Clear.
See image.

blocks.item: Go to your local system and paste as necessary.

blocks.text: Certain browsers support the Clipboard paste function in a privileged console using your own keyboard. From your own keyboard, use the keys associated with pasting for the related machine. To learn more, see Browser Behavior. When your browser doesn't allow the Clipboard paste function with your keyboard, use the following steps:

blocks.item: Copy content from your local system. When Clipboard is enabled, the copied content is periodically synced to the privileged console Clipboard if the browser you are using supports it.

blocks.text: You can copy and paste up to 4,096 characters by default. If you need a larger clipboard size, you can request an increase of up to 32K characters by contacting Zscaler Support.

blocks.item: Go to the privileged console and navigate to where you want to paste into the privileged console.

blocks.text: Websites or other applications on your device can modify the Clipboard before it is pasted into the privileged console. Ensure the content is not modified before pasting it into your privileged console.

blocks.item: Click the Clipboard icon at the bottom of the screen.

blocks.text: The Clipboard window appears.
If you have a current session running and you start Clipboard, then you must terminate the existing session and start a new session to show the Clipboard icon.
The text is pasted into the Clipboard window within the privileged console.
See image.
When the Clipboard Copy and Paste features are enabled, the Clipboard functions are dependent upon the browser you are using.

If you are using Safari, you can only use the Clipboard window to do copy and paste operations within the privileged console. When using Safari, the browser's Copy and Paste buttons appear next to the Clipboard Copy and Paste buttons.
See image.

If you are using Chrome and have copied from the local system Clipboard and are pasting into the privileged console, a pop-up message from your Chrome browser appears when you attempt the paste operation by keyboard or via the privileged console Clipboard. Click Allow to complete the paste.
See image.

If you are using Firefox and want to copy from a privileged console and paste into the Firefox browser, you can use either the Clipboard window or the keyboard.
